sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006)
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF; §§3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.3 and 5.3, PDF pp. 10–19; local state and first-law argument especially §4.3 equations (4.10)–(4.14), PDF pp. 15–17.

contents.name: Local state variables, rest energy and derivative-defined quantities

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete §4.3 reasoning from the local equation-of-state assumption and rest-energy decomposition (4.10)–(4.11), through the fixed-comoving-volume first law (4.12)–(4.13) and derivative definitions (4.14).
source_review.supports: Rest-frame state variables, total energy including rest mass, and the selected fluid model's derivative definitions for temperature and chemical potential.
source_review.limitations: The source uses its chosen multicomponent fluid framework and c=1 chemical-potential notation. This item adopts a supplied single-material C2 state function, restores mc² in SI, and does not treat the source as an empirical equation of state or proof of universal material behavior.

contents.name: Lorentzian geometry, local observer and stress-energy conventions

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete relevant definitions in §§3.1–3.2 and §§4.1–4.2, PDF pp. 10–15, including the unit timelike flow and comoving stress-energy components.
source_review.supports: Independent lecture-note context for a future timelike flow, a pointwise local rest frame, tensor-valued stress-energy, and rest-frame thermodynamic quantities.
source_review.limitations: The assigned definition uses the exact local congruence and tensor interfaces of its linked mathematical suppliers. The source's global fluid equations and its perfect-fluid assumptions are not imported.

contents.name: Perfect-fluid entropy and circulation discussion
contents.reason: The source's perfect-fluid conservation conclusions require its own fluid equations; the assigned entropy postulate instead explicitly adopts a selected current inequality and does not infer it from those equations.

sources.title: Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (version 2015)

contents.name: Local thermodynamic equilibrium as a restricted continuum-model assumption

source_review.read_extent: Read §I.1.3 in full, including its finite-cell and slow-variation qualifications for local equilibrium.
source_review.supports: Local equilibrium is a modeling regime whose use requires declared scale and applicability conditions.
source_review.limitations: The assigned postulate keeps the equation of state supplied and does not infer microscopic validity or a particular real material from these notes.

contents.name: Relativistic flow, local rest quantities and current/tensor decompositions

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete local-rest-flow discussion in §IX.2, the current and stress setup in §IX.3.1, and the decompositions and frame distinctions in §§IX.4.1–IX.4.2, PDF pp. 137–147.
source_review.supports: An independent treatment of future timelike flow, comoving variables, current and tensor types, and distinct local frame choices.
source_review.limitations: The notes use c=k_B=1 in parts and explicitly warn that some derivations are incomplete. The item retains SI units and uses the source only for conventions, not as a proof or universal constitutive law.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes (12 October 2022 revision)
sources.locator: Full 125-page PDF; §5.3, PDF pp. 56–57, Killing equation and current-divergence exercise; §6.3, PDF pp. 64–66, observer energy and stress-energy.

contents.name: Killing-current divergence and finite charge context

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §5.3 Killing-current exercise and §6.3 observer-energy discussion in the full PDF; the current calculation uses symmetry of the stress tensor and Killing's equation.
source_review.supports: Independent general-relativity treatment of the current and observer-energy conventions used by the assigned finite matter-charge definition.
source_review.limitations: The authored physical theorem depends on the exact finite-coordinate-box MI01 supplier and proves no global or gravitational energy result.

contents.name: Global Stokes theorem discussion
contents.reason: The assigned proof applies the current draft finite-box theorem, not Reall's global Stokes theorem or a non-null unit-normal formula for each side face.

sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted chapter 4 section HTML; §4.5.5, Conserved Energy from a Killing Vector, current divergence and hypersurface charge.

contents.name: Killing stress-energy current and hypersurface charge

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete author-hosted §4.5.5, including its current definition, covariant divergence calculation, finite hypersurface charge and the condition on boundary flux.
source_review.supports: A second independent lecture-note treatment of the Killing current and charge convention alongside Reall.
source_review.limitations: The assigned local proof keeps its own sign, normal orientation, units and draft mathematical finite-slab interface.

sources.title: The International System of Units (SI), BIPM, 9th edition, version 4.01 (2026)
sources.locator: §2.2, PDF pp. 124–125: SI defining constants, exact values and the relation between numerical values and unit definitions.

contents.name: SI constants c, h and k_B

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the full 214-page current BIPM brochure and read §2.2, including the exact defining-constant table and its unit-definition explanation.
source_review.supports: The SI status of c, Planck's constant h, and the Boltzmann constant k_B as exact defining constants.
source_review.limitations: This is metrological evidence about SI definitions, not a derivation of physical model postulates or of an equation of state.

sources.title: P. J. Mohr, D. B. Newell, and B. N. Taylor, CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022, NIST
sources.locator: CODATA 2022 adjustment discussion and input table for the Newtonian constant of gravitation G; no numerical value is reproduced.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the full-text CODATA 2022 reference and its G input-data table, which reports experiments and standard uncertainty.
source_review.supports: G is an experimentally adjusted constant rather than one of the exact defining constants of the SI.
source_review.limitations: No numerical G value or precision is asserted in this item.

sources.title: Paul Romatschke, New Developments in Relativistic Viscous Hydrodynamics, arXiv:0906.4787v2 (2010)
sources.locator: Full 25-page PDF; §4.1, PDF pp. 9–10, conformal non-equilibrium entropy current, its divergence and source limitation.

source_review.read_extent: Read all of §4.1 through its displayed entropy-current divergence (4.2) and the discussion immediately following it.
source_review.supports: The use of a nonnegative entropy-current divergence as a model condition in a specified relativistic-fluid branch; the author explicitly says he knows of no experimental verification of that hypothesis.
source_review.limitations: The calculation is for the paper's conformal-fluid expansion. It does not prove a universal local second law, supply an empirical test, or establish the assigned theorem.

contents.name: Generalized entropy, horizon entropy and observations
contents.reason: No horizon-area term, exterior quantum entropy, measurement, or generalized second law is used in the finite material-current deduction.
